cohort: 1000 figures, one per patent, drawn from filter_manifest_v3 'drawing' rows, disjoint from the curated 100; no content decisions exist for them

execution.reading: 80.7% against 86% on the curated cohort, so the curated 100 was mildly optimistic but broadly representative

timing_seconds.reading: median 15.0s, better than the curated cohort's 33s because the median patent figure is simpler, but the tail is heavy: p90 is 72s and the worst figure took 1061s, essentially all of it Stage 2.

defect_found_only_at_scale.what: 13 figures (1.3%) died with CUDA out-of-memory in Stage 0 OCR
defect_found_only_at_scale.why: large scans at 10 workers across 2 cards; the curated 100 never triggered it
defect_found_only_at_scale.fix: a CPU reader now catches the OOM and finishes that figure, so the run completes instead of losing real drawings to a placement choice
defect_found_only_at_scale.note: this is exactly what a dry run is for and is the only new failure mode volume exposed

acceptance.reading: content_manifest_absent fires on 100% of figures because none has a human content decision. Acceptance is fail-closed and Phase D is confirmed as the binding constraint on scale, not anything in the pipeline.

roadmap_rule: F1 says anything firing on more than 10% of figures gets treatment before F2. Excluding content (Phase D) and the validation-missing family (a consequence of non-execution), that leaves the Stage-2 gate at 13.7% -- which is the max_edges question already queued as the next item.

holding_at_scale.note: the run-length fix holds: 1.8% at scale against 55% before it

corpus_projection.note: median 15s at 10 workers is roughly 2400 figures/hour, so ~78k figures is about 1.4 days of wall clock, but the heavy tail makes that optimistic
